request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 2 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. (Independent run 3.)

concerns: Run 3 beats run 1 by 0.0576 PR-AUC, which is under one SD (about 0.06), so the gain is not clearly real. Run 3 beats run 2 by only 0.0345, well within one SD.

The simplicity rule favors logistic (run 1) unless a complex model wins by more than 1 SD. No complex model clears that bar against run 1 (the largest gap, 0.0576, is just under SD 0.0595-0.0617). Run 2 is not simpler than logistic, so it is carried forward only as a hedge; treat the logistic baseline as the fallback if no later run is clearly better.

The PotentialFraud label has an undocumented origin and may reflect a prior audit rule or a rule-derived flag, so the high ROC-AUC (about 0.94) and PR-AUC (about 0.7) may reflect label leakage or proxy features rather than real fraud detection. Even a plain logistic model on 50 features reaches 0.94, which is suspicious.
Size features (volume and counts) may act as proxies for the labeling mechanism; the no_size ablation was run only for logistic and LightGBM with confounded settings.

Agent features are 19 aggregate ratios, and their effect is confounded with the imbalance setting and the model in runs 3 and 4. Run 4 differs from run 3 in several ways at once, so no single factor can be isolated.
Fold SD of about 0.06-0.076 is large with only about 506 positives, so the ranking among runs is noisy. Precision@50 differences of 0.02-0.06 amount to 1-3 providers.
The queue is about 100 providers but only precision@50 is reported, so precision at the real queue size is unknown. Claims cover one year, so temporal generalization is untested.

next_experiments.rationale: Isolates the agent-feature effect in the simplest model, to test whether the gain comes from the features or from LightGBM.
A more regularized version of run 3, to check whether its edge holds with less capacity and under the noise.
A strongly regularized, simple baseline with size included, to test the size-proxy and leakage concern.
